newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says Honda to build new motorcycle plant.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says Honda to build new motorcycle plant.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd plans to build a new motorcycle plant in Brazil's Goais state, with a total start-up cost of $300 million, said Brazilian Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles.
Dornelles said Honda, which will benefit from special fiscal incentives for setting up in Brazil's center-west region, intends to reach annual production of 150,000 bikes a year within five years.
He said construction would begin in 1998 and that installation costs were $70 million while other expenses associated with the start-up reach $230 million.
"It is calculated that this will generate 1,000 jobs," Dornelles told repoters.
He said Honda would benefit from a special decree granting fiscal incentives to car makers who set up factories in the impoverished northeast or the interior, including Goias state.
Dornelles said that Honda is already building an automobile plant whose costs include $100 million for installation and $300 million in start-up capital.
He said the manufacturer would begin marketing its locally built Civic model in October, the first units to roll off its new factory in Sumare, outside Sao Paulo.
